key_insight: Entanglement enables perfectly private quantum communication advantages for concrete functions, but three-bit AND requires more than one qubit per player within the studied encoding model.
engineering_relevance: These results identify communication savings and local-dimension requirements for designing noninteractive secure multiparty quantum protocols.
method: Construct entanglement-assisted protocols for three-party equality and three-bit majority.
Prove a three-bit AND impossibility for shared three-qubit states with local unitary encodings.
Construct GHZ-based qutrit and higher-dimensional qudit protocols for AND.
evidence_signal: Theoretical constructions and lower bounds show equality costs asymptotically 1.633…n qubits versus at least 3n without entanglement, majority costs 3 qubits versus 6 classical bits, and three-bit AND costs 3 log₂ 3 qubits versus 6 classical bits.
watch_item: The AND impossibility is restricted to the stated three-qubit local-unitary model; hardware noise and entanglement-distribution costs are not evaluated in the abstract.
paper_title: Concrete Functions in Private Simultaneous Quantum Messages: Quantum Advantages and Structural Limitations
